summary:
Open-world audit, kid's-eye view. I ran a naive bot on the live configuration: iPad touch, 1024x768 (3.0 pt per game px), with warm-up, phrases and listen-and-do all ON. The bot only taps what is visible on screen. It played from a new game through the opener ("¡A explorar!"), a 15-minute day 1 (first zone, La casa de los abuelos, reached by the path), a forced sunset to bed, day 2 with the warm-up, and about 4 minutes of Villa Sol chapters. Targeted runs then covered the bus stop and world map, a listen favour (Don Pepe), and Lola's carry request on the beach.

What works: when the guide isn't caught in a loop it works very well. On day 2, chapters c3 to c6 lost 0 s, and every next step was found by following the arrow. The whole zone story (abuelos1-3) was completed from arrows alone. The path from town to the first zone took about 9 s. All 6 tap points on the town bus sign open the bus, and a ride takes 3.9 s. The warm-up took 15.7 s for 4 picture cards with a skip button. No question had more than 4 choices. Listen-and-do and the carry requests never dead-end: a child who doesn't understand still finished the beach request in 50 s.

Biggest weaknesses:
- **Two guide loops on the live config.** Choosing "¡A explorar!" sends the child in and out of the front door (49 trips in 60 s). On the first zone visit, Lola's heart bubble replays the same 4-line greeting for about 229 s (45 times).
- **Mostly talk, little exploring.** About 85-94% of a guide-following child's time is dialogue and questions, at about 7 questions a minute. Single talks run up to 10 pages plus 11 questions.
- **The menu button covers a bus stop.** At the grandparents' place the bus-stop sign sits under the menu button (the word-card deck) in the top-right corner, so tapping it opens the menu.
- **The world map has no tappable goal and no arrow.** The letter picture can't be tapped, and the child's own pick of a new place is overruled by the letter errand.
- **A 15-minute child never reaches sunset**, which comes after 18 minutes in one sitting. So bed, the "¡Hoy!" recap and "buenas noches" are never seen, and the recap only counts the current sitting.
- **About 43% of day-1 questions use word-only cards**, so she has to read Spanish.

Both loops slipped through because the test harness turns phrases, listen-and-do and the warm-up off by default, and the explore-branch test's check is too loose. The repo was not changed.

findings.title: Choosing '¡A explorar!' in the opener traps the child in an endless in-and-out loop at the front door
findings.evidence: Reproduced from a new game through the real UI twice (runs A and B1). In the house, guide.at = 'explore playa': the arrow is on the door (key/01a_explore_loop_house_arrow_out.png). Out in town, guide.at = 'job in casa': the arrow is back on the house door (key/01b_..., key/01c_explore_loop_town_arrow.png). Following the arrow gave 49 door trips in 60 s (runB/b.json 'explore loop'). Root cause: guide.js:143 (reviewGoal) suggests 'job in <map>' whenever E.waitsIn(map), and chapters.js:398-402 CH.waitsIn('casa') is true because the deferred puppy chapter c1 has its giver, Mamá, in the house. Inside the house the same chapter is deliberately skipped (guide.js:141 'n.id !== later', guide.js:158 puppyLater), so the house goal falls through to exploreGoal, i.e. the door. The only escape is tapping Mamá's puppy bubble, which starts the puppy tutorial she just declined. tools/test-world.js:50 only checks !/c1:/ on the why, so 'job in casa' passes.
findings.impact: Every child who picks the explore picture, the very first choice in the game, follows the arrow straight into a loop. It's the 'don't know what to do' complaint again, on minute one. Explorers end up doing the puppy tutorial anyway (time to first zone was about 4 min in run A).
findings.fix: In guide.js reviewGoal, skip E.waitsIn maps whose only reason is a not-started chapter. Either give CH.waitsIn an option to ignore lives() that aren't started, or apply the puppyLater/'later' exclusion there too. Tighten test-world.js:50 to require /^explore /. Add a naive-bot loop check: the same pair of (map, guide.why) alternating 3 times or more fails the test.

findings.title: Lola's heart bubble replays the same greeting about 45 times on the first zone visit and hides the zone's story
findings.evidence: Run A, day 1, La casa de los abuelos, t259 to t488: the guide said 'bubble lola' for about 229 s. Each tap replayed '¡[hola], Luz! / ¡La casa de los abuelos! / ¡Mira, Canelo! / ¡Tus abuelos! ¡Entra!' (45 repeats, 180 of the day's 286 pages; runA/log-A.json; key/02_lola_heart_bubble_loop.png). Root cause: phrases.js:704 shows Lola's heart bubble (P.favBubble) whenever P.favReady(), i.e. 3 album animals met. But favTalk (phrases.js:640-643) calls P.request('f_gusta'), which returns null while P.canIntro is false. That is the case for P.GAP = 240 s after another pattern (phrases.js:53/350), and 'Me llamo' is introduced by Lola herself on arrival. So the talk falls back to her hello (zones.js:415-418) and the bubble never clears. Meanwhile the zone's own story (abuelos1, 'chapterLater') ranks below 'bubble lola' in guide.js:171 TIERS, so the arrow never leads into the house she keeps telling the child to enter.
findings.impact: This hits essentially every child on her first zone visit: about 4 minutes of a 15-minute session hearing the same 4 lines, with the arrow pinned on Lola. It reads as broken and exactly reproduces 'didn't know what to do next'.
findings.fix: Make Lola's alert require that the talk can actually run: (P.met('f_gusta') || P.canIntro('f_gusta', {slots: albumMet()})). In general, an NPC's alert() and talk() should share one 'can run now' predicate. Also run tools/test-zone-*.js and naivebot with PHRASES=1 LISTEN=1 WARMUP=1.

findings.title: About 85-94% of a guide-following child's time is dialogue and quizzes; single talks reach 10 pages + 11 questions
findings.evidence: Instrumented every scene between free moments (runA/log-A.json, runA2/log-A2.json). Day 2, chapters c3-c6 (Villa Sol, 240 s of game time): 79 pages and 55 questions in scenes, against 42 s free on the map. Estimated child time (speech per page plus about 4 s per question): about 650 s in scenes versus 42 s walking. Day 1 zone story (abuelos, t500-735): 54 pages and 44 questions (about 7 a minute) versus 82 s free. Densest single talks: Don Pepe's sí/no game, 10 pages + 11 questions in one conversation (A2 burst 'day2 5'). c1 puppy: 9 pages + 7 questions (about 55 s). Simón dice: 6 pages + 8 questions. Static count of later chapters: c20 Sofía's beat asks 8 questions in a row (story-c11-c21.js:993-1003), Luna's opening beat asks 7 (lines 961-972), and c20/c21 have 28/22 asks across 4/2 beats.
findings.impact: The child loves exploring, animals and the dog, but on the arrow's path the map is only about 6-15% of her time. Long question chains between actions are where a 7-year-old taps through without listening, and where 'boring' comes from.
findings.fix: Cap questions at 3 per conversation before something physical happens on the map (walk, carry, find, the dog acts). Split dense beats into map steps (e.g. c20's ribbons become 4 ribbons to pick up). Move the sí/no game into the world (Pepe holds up things as you walk past his stall). Add a per-beat budget check to a test: max pages and max questions between free moments.

findings.title: At the grandparents' place the bus-stop sign sits under the menu button; tapping what the arrow points at opens the menu
findings.evidence: runB2/b.json: with the player at (22,5) on map abuelos, the bus sign is at screen (304,20), inside the menu/deck button (294-314, 6-26; field.js:6 HUD). A tap on the sign opens 'FieldMenu', not the bus (key/03a_bus_sign_under_menu_button.png, key/03b_tap_on_bus_opens_menu.png). At (22,6) the sign is off the top (y=-4), and the guide's up-arrow at (304,30) points straight at the menu button (key/03c_arrow_points_at_menu_button.png). In run A2 the bot following 'letter to mama (bus)' ended up in FieldMenu exactly this way. Abuelos' bus stop is at tile (28,2), near the top-right of the map (zone-abuelos.js:1059).
findings.impact: Tomás's letters send her to the bus every day once a zone is visited. A child who taps the arrow's target gets the card menu instead of the bus, again and again: a 'the game ignores me' moment.
findings.fix: Keep map targets out from under the HUD. Either let the camera scroll so the top 2 rows can sit below y=32, or move the abuelos stop down a few rows. In field.js, when a tap hits the HUD button but the guide's target lies under it, let the target win. Also keep the guide's up-arrow from being placed on HUD rectangles.

findings.title: World map: the letter picture can't be tapped, there's no arrow, and the child's own pick of a new place is overruled by the letter errand
findings.evidence: Runs A2 and B. The letter badge is drawn at node.x - r - 16 (connect.js:339-340, 22x22), while the place's tap rect starts at x - r - 2 (zones.js:444). Tapping the letter picture left the map open with nothing happening (log-A2 events: 'tapped the letter picture beside villa → WorldMap', twice). key/04a_world_map_letter_badge_not_tappable.png. The world map has no guide arrow (hintXY null). Tapping an unvisited '?' place (La playa) sets want='playa' and shows footprints, but back on the map the arrow points to Mamá for the letter (postGoal ranks above wantGoal, guide.js:171). key/04b_asked_for_beach_arrow_goes_to_letter.png.
findings.impact: On the letter-by-bus trips (which earlier made the harness bot loop for 2.7 min), the most obvious thing to tap does nothing. When she does choose where to explore, the game ignores her choice, which undercuts the open-world promise.
findings.fix: Make the letter badge part of its place's tap rect (or its own target). Add the guide's bouncing arrow over the destination node on the world map. Rank wantGoal above postGoal (or drop 'want' only when she arrives).

findings.title: A 15-minute-a-day child never sees sunset, bed or the '¡Hoy!' recap; the recap only counts the current sitting
findings.evidence: day.js:12 SUNSET_AT = 18*60 s of play since the game was opened, and day.js:21-23 resets the session on every load. Run A at 15 min: sessionTime 914, sunsetAt 1080 (event 'day 1 at 15 min'). After reloading and going to bed (sunset forced), the Hoy card showed no words, only '¡Muy bien, Luz!' (key/05_hoy_card_empty_after_reopen.png, run A2), because DY.today() is 'since the session began'.
findings.impact: The evening ritual (going home, buenas noches, today's word cards growing), the only end-of-day reflection on what she learned, is designed for sittings longer than the target 15 minutes. Most real sittings end mid-errand with no closure.
findings.fix: Tie sunset to the session plan: about 12-13 min of play, or after the day's main chapter. Compute 'today' by calendar date from G.state.hist (it already records words met per day), not the in-memory session base. Let the grown-ups' menu set the session length.

findings.title: About 43% of day-1 questions use word-only cards, so the child must read Spanish; abuela/abuelo/bebé differ by one letter
findings.evidence: runA/log-A.json Choice records: 36 of 83 day-1 questions had no picture on any card (learn.js Choice.view textOnly). Examples: '¿Quién es?' ['bebe','abuela','abuelo'] three times in a row (burst 'day1 112', photo wall); '¿Qué es?' ['pantalon','camisa','vestido'] minutes after first meeting them; 'Lola: ¡...!' ['hola','uno','manzana'] (key/13_word_only_cards_hola_uno_manzana.png).
findings.impact: She reads English, not Spanish. Telling abuela from abuelo by its last letter is close to a coin flip, so these 'recall' items turn into guessing on day 1. The parent asked for picture and word together.
findings.fix: For words met under about 2 days ago, use picture+word cards (recognition). Allow word-only cards only once a word reaches stage 3+ and the distractors differ in their first letters. Never put abuela/abuelo or other one-letter-apart pairs together on word-only cards.

findings.title: Overlaps: Canelo's '?' bubble hides a puzzle's choice arrow; the held-item label covers the top of the map; popups cover the first arrows
findings.evidence: Geometric check at every free moment plus screenshots. (1) 'Who says ¡Cuac!?' (c6): the white choice arrow over Canelo is fully under his own '?' review bubble (100% overlap). The child sees one arrow (ducks) plus a '?' meaning something else on the same dog (key/06a_canelo_question_bubble_hides_choice_arrow.png, A2 t197). (2) The held-item label at the top-left ('los calcetines ↓' + letter) covers the top rows where a guide arrow was pointing, and a word bubble with its mic floats mid-garden (key/06b_carry_hud_over_top_arrow_and_word_bubble.png, A t670; dog-spot bubble vs arrow 32%). (3) '¡Nuevo animal!' (album.js:244, 170 frames) covers the very first arrow over the house door after the opener (key/01b...). (4) At sunset at the abuelos bus stop, the edge arrow, moon badge, bus sign and a speech bubble sit within about 60 px (key/06c_evening_cluster_arrow_moon_bus_bubble.png). (5) A growing word card covers the right third of the map during hide-and-seek (key/06d_word_card_over_map_during_seek.png).
findings.impact: Two cues on one target with different meanings, or a cue hidden under a label, is exactly where a pre-reader taps the wrong thing or stalls.
findings.fix: Suppress NPC alert bubbles on any NPC that is currently a guide choice target. Draw the held-item label (errands drawHud) below y=32, or shrink it when an arrow or target falls under it. Delay '¡Nuevo animal!' and word-card popups while the guide arrow is within their rectangle, or place them on the opposite half of the screen.

findings.title: Carry request (e.g. 'Tráeme tres conchas'): the ear bubble keeps re-asking while the arrows to the piles wait for 10 s of standing still
findings.evidence: runB3/b.json: on the beach, a child who doesn't understand the words tapped Lola's ear bubble 8 times (each tap repeats the request). The guide stayed '[hidden]' (quiz goal, guide.js layout: 'g.quiz && idle < IDLE_SOFT', 600 frames). The pile arrows appeared only after 15.2 s of wandering and standing (moment 20). The request was done after 50.3 s. key/07_carry_request_lola_repeats.png.
findings.impact: An active child never stands still for 10 s, so the only cue she sees is the person she just talked to. Re-asking a Spanish sentence she didn't understand teaches nothing and feels like a loop.
findings.fix: After the first repeat, have Lola point (CH.point) at the piles, or show the choice arrows on all piles immediately (they're a choice, so they don't give the answer away). Count taps on the requester as 'idle' for the hint timer.

findings.title: The test harness turns the live features off by default, so the regression suite doesn't play the game children get
findings.evidence: tools/harness.js:19-26: warm-up, phrases and listen-and-do are OFF unless a test passes {warmup|phrases|listen:true} or WARMUP/PHRASES/LISTEN=1. In the live game they are on (phrases.js:63 P.on, listen.js:40 L.off only reads those test flags). naivebot.js and audit-intuitive.js open pages without them, and playflow's newGame never picks 'explore'. Both critical loops above appear only in the live configuration and the explore branch.
findings.impact: Guide regressions caused by phrases (the Lola loop) and the explore branch (the door loop) passed 1630/1630 checks and reached the live game.
findings.fix: Add a live-config job to tools/test-all.sh: smoke + test-guide + a 10-minute naive-bot run with WARMUP=1 PHRASES=1 LISTEN=1, once with play and once with explore, failing on any (map, guide.why) ping-pong or the same talk repeated 3+ times without progress.

findings.title: Hide-and-seek finds take 17-21 s because the arrow waits for 10 s of standing still
findings.evidence: Run A, abuelos: 'seek pavo' found after 21.5 s (idle 8, wander 10.4); 'seek gato' after 17 s (idle 7.3, wander 9.3) while the cat was visible on the henhouse roof (key/06d..., key/12_seek_edge_arrow.png). The edge arrow points the way, but over the hider it only appears after IDLE_SOFT = 600 frames.
findings.impact: Mostly fine (finding is the fun part), but a moving child resets the timer. The playtest favourite is also the moment where the bot lost the most real seconds.
findings.fix: Use cumulative seconds since the round started, not continuous idleness, for the soft arrow (e.g. 20 s), and make the hider's peek bigger and livelier as time passes.

metrics:
**Setup:** iPad touch page 1024x768, canvas 960x672 = **3.0 pt per game px**. Tap targets measured: buttons 20 px (60 pt), padded to 28 px (84 pt); letter cells 20x22; listen-and-do cells 54x62; seek hit areas 28 px wide. The only failures found are the HUD-covered bus stop and the letter badge on the world map. Warm-up, phrases and listen-and-do were all ON, as in the live game.

**Opener:** 11.4 s of game time (about 30 s for a child), 7 pages (3 with no picture), 1 question, 17 taps. Keeping the dog's default name takes 1 tap on ✓.

**Explore choice:** 49 door trips in 60 s following the arrow; the loop never ends on its own.

**Day 1, 15 minutes (sessionTime 914 s):**
- **Where it went:** c1, c2, the first zone (abuelos) and its whole story (abuelos1-3), the vegetable garden, Simón dice, the family photo, Nico's hide-and-seek, and a letter from Tomás. 27 words met.
- **Getting to the zone:** the path took 9 s (4.7 s in town to the edge, 4.3 s on camino_abuelos).
- **Volume:** 286 pages, of which 180 were the Lola loop repeats; 83 questions; 185 free moments.
- **Lola loop:** 45 repeats over about 229 s.
- **Real lost seconds:** about 70 s, mostly hide-and-seek (21.5 s and 17 s). Another 139 s came from my loop-breaker.
- **Overlaps flagged:** 2 on day 1, 2 on day 2. At most 3 bubbles on screen at once.
- **Choice sizes:** 1 card ×8, 2 ×1, 3 ×64, 4 ×10. Nothing over 4.

**Share of a child's time in scenes** (estimated: about 1.2 s + 0.5 s per word per page, plus 4 s per question):

| Segment | Pages | Questions | Free on map | Share free |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Abuelos story (t500-735) | 54 | 44 | 82 s | ~15% |
| Villa Sol c3-c6 (day 2) | 79 | 55 | 42 s | ~6% |

- **Densest single talk:** 10 pages + 11 questions.

**Bus:** all 6 tap points around the town sign open the bus. A ride takes 3.9 s from tap to free. Tapping the letter badge on the world map does nothing (2 of 2 tries).

**Evening:** after a forced sunset, bed was reached in 13 s. The Hoy card was empty after a reopen. Natural sunset comes after 1080 s in one sitting, longer than a 15-minute session.

**Day 2 warm-up:** 15.7 s, 4 items (zapatos, sombrero, boca, Me llamo), recognition with picture cards, 3 of 4 counted right.

**Listen-and-do:**
- Don Pepe: found in 2 s; the request was 'Dame cinco manzanas.' with 3 piles.
- Lola on the beach ('Tráeme tres conchas.'): done in 50.3 s by a child who doesn't understand the words. She was re-asked 8 times, and the pile arrows appeared after 15.2 s.

**How fast content goes:**

| | Bot time | Child estimate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One zone story (3 chapters + side quests) | ~4 min | ~9 min (under one session) |
| One Villa Sol chapter (c3-c6) | ~60 s | ~2.7 min |

Extrapolation (estimate): the 36 written chapters are about 1.7-2 h of child time, roughly 7-8 sessions of 15 min. With the daily 'tomorrow' gates that is roughly 2-4 weeks of play, against about 1,000 sessions in 3 years.

**Files** (all under `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Spanish-Club/56c6d0c5-5673-5d69-87f4-ad0ff9c7afaf/scratchpad/audit2/openworld/`):
- `ow-audit.js` and `ow-b.js`: the audit scripts.
- `runA/log-A.json`, `runA2/log-A2.json`, `runB/b.json`, `runB2/b.json`, `runB3/b.json`: per-moment and per-scene logs.
- `key/`: the 22 key screenshots referenced in the findings.
